title: Annotatio VI §.I: Apostle (1 Cor 11) on latter — judgment; not discerning the body
pass_a_gloss: Of these latter the Apostle treated expressly in the said Corinthian chapter, saying that by eating of the Sacred bread and drinking of the cup they become guilty of Christ’s body itself, and eat and drink judgment to themselves — at minimum temporal — i.e. fall into heavier diseases, sometimes followed by temporal death itself, plainly for this cause: that they do not discern Christ’s body, or fly to the sacred feast no otherwise than to eat common food.
pass_b_english: Paul’s Corinthian chapter treats these latter expressly: eating the sacred bread and drinking the cup, they become guilty of the body and eat/drink judgment — at least temporal sickness, sometimes death.
Cause: they do not discern Christ’s body, or rush the sacred meal as if it were common food.
source_text: De posterioribus hisce ex professo egit Apostolus, dictô ad Corinthios capite, dicens, quòd manducando de pane Sacro, bibendóque de poculo, ipsius corporis Christi rei fiant, & judicium, ad minimum temporale, sibi edant & bibant, i. e. in morbos graviores incidant, subsequente quandoque ipsâ morte temporali, eam planè ob causam, quòd non discernunt corpus Christi, vel ad sacrum epulum non aliter advolant, quàm ad communem cibum manducandum.

lemmas.gloss: they do not discern Christ’s body
